messages.subject: Re: I would need your hints, advices and experience for building bilingual apps.
messages.subject_clean: I would need your hints, advices and experience for building bilingual apps.
messages.body_plain:
Hi Grégoire and Joe.
Thank you very much for your contributions. I'll take advantage of them.
I've isolated a bit the root of the problem. Unfortunately, I was not able to go further.
It's something related with withMathJax when it's on the server side. If the call is made
from the ui side, everything works well. Obviously, it's not a matter on performance, as
I pointed out the first time.

The ui code is something like: uiOutput("test")   (among some other similar functions)

On the other side:
  output$test = renderUI({
    withMathJax( p('\\(= \\sum_j \\sum_i (y_{i,j} - \\bar{Y})^2 \\)'))
  } )

Notice that this is simpler tan real: no translations here, though this doesn't make a difference, I guess.
Actually, the page loads this with no problems: the headache is related with its interferences with
other blocks, which don't appear, or appear after refreshing the page, or not appear at all.

I'm aware that I'm not including relevant information here. I would ask for help to anyone which
experienced problems with MathJax once, or they know about documentation on mathJax + Shiny.
Or simply stay tuned until I made some progress.

Well, merci bien tous les deux

JA

El viernes, 30 de octubre de 2015, 18:25:17 (UTC+1), José Antonio González escribió:
> I've written already some twenty apps of considerable size, almost all of them in Spanish, but I'm considering to include an English
> version. I've discarded a second copy with texts in English, because of expected problems in maintenance of two versions. I'd like
> to have a language selector in the same app, and swap the texts dynamically.
>
> However, after some tests with an app, complex enough for finding different kind of difficulties, I give up. Inexplicably at least for me,
> the two-language version was making its way until a point where it was behaving unpredictably. Some parts (texts or plots) don't
> appear but if I refresh the page in the browser (I'm using a remote server, not Rstudio), it can appear complete, perhaps... Even
> worse, sometimes the load finishes with an error message, but after refreshing the page loads partially or maybe totally.
>
> I have to explain that this behaviour has not appeared at some critical point. I was advancing slowly, writing small pieces of code
> and checking them carefully before facing another piece. The first times I noticed that the error was not a real error I thought that
> the reason could be a mismatch between the remote server and my computer, and the upload was not complete when I tried to
> refresh the page (it would be strange anyway, since the files are really small).
>
> As I was advancing in the implementation of the two-language version, obviously the program was increasing in complexity. I wonder
> if this can have influence in the app behaviour: I had to convert a number of simple p('blablabla'), HTML('blablabla') and widgets in
> renderText and renderUI calls (because of the language dependency), BUT it would be hard to accept that functions like that are
> able to degrade the program so much.
>
> So I think that I should return to the starting point, and adopt a different paradigm. I've sought a bit about the topic, but it seems
> that translations are not very common, or they don't pose any problem normally. In my case, my initial strategy is:
> a global environment (.E), with a variable to store the selected language (d): each language has an actionButton, and an observer to update the variable (.E$d)
> a global list of character arrays; each array with the expression in English and in Spanish
> Examples of use:
>   output$titulo = renderText( { .L$titulo[.E$d] } )
>   output$par2 = renderUI( { HTML(.L$par2[.E$d]) } )
>   output$Type = renderUI({    radioButtons("tipo", .L$pastel[.E$d], c(.L$pie1[.E$d], .L$pie2[.E$d]), inline=TRUE)  })
> Perhaps a clue: I'm using withMathJax too. Is it so toxic that it could be related to that undesirable performance?
>
> Have you any similar experience? Can you propose any other strategy? I will appreciate it so much.
>
> JA
>
>

Hello experienced shiny developers,

I need to plot different graphs depending on the user input, so I have
 verticalLayout(

                     tableOutput("countTable_one"),
                     tableOutput("countTable_two"),

                    # first conditional panel
                     conditionalPanel("input.xx1.length ==1",
                                       showOutput("xxbar", "nvd3")

                     ),
                    # second conditional panel
                     conditionalPanel("input.xx1.length ==2",
                                       fluidRow(column(6,showOutput("xxbar", "nvd3"),plotOutput("nullplot1",width="auto")),
                                                column(6,showOutput("xxbartwo", "nvd3")))

                     ),
                      fluid = T)
        ),

It works with either only the first conditional panel or the second, but not if I have both. If I had both conditions in, all conditional inputs are messed up, i.e: only the common inputs will be shown.

Any idea or suggestion how to fix this?

Thank you in advance!

messages.subject: Functions as reactive conductors
messages.subject_clean: Functions as reactive conductors
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

This is a post in response to the article on Reactivity:

shiny.rstudio.com/articles/reactivity-overview.html <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/reactivity-overview.html>

I read this article in detail before trying to implement a conductor (to speed up my calculations by only doing them once).
I initially tried to set up the code in the way specified in the code example just above the Summary section:
"On the other hand, if currentFib is a function that accesses a reactive value, and that function is called within the reactive world, then it will work:"

This did not work; the calculations still ended up being re-run every time. Even though the function was being called by renderPlot and by renderText, as in the example above, and the function itself was calling the reactive elements.

When I changed by calculation from a function to a reactive element, then everything worked.
So my problem is not that the reactivity didn't work, but that the alternative example you gave that should have also worked, did not work.
The *only* thing I changed was to change the calculations from a function into a reactive element.

My app is https://lmcm177.shinyapps.io/genechart-upload

I don't know whether there are other things I needed to do to get run_geneplot_calcs to work as a function instead of as a reactive, but the reactivity didn't work when it was a function. So it would be helpful if you either removed that example from the article, or explained why it might not have worked as an alternative to a reactive element.

Thanks,

Louise

messages.body_plain:
Not sure if this is a recommended way of doing this, but it might work: in the `mySerialisedApp.R` file, you can return a Shiny app object, like this:

mySerialisedApp.R
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage("I'm a shiny app")

server <- function(input, output, session) {}

shinyApp(ui, server)

And when you want to run it from a different file, you could `source()` , which will return the Shiny app as an object, so you could do

source("mySerialisedApp.R")$value

I think that'd work. Hopefully that's what you were looking for.

As I said, I don't know how encouraged this solution is, so use at your own risk.

I am definitely not an advanced shiny user but I have sort of a similar goal as I try to keep track of user interactions with the app.

You have probably already tried these, but just in case:

First thing that came to mind was to add some commands at the end of each function that would append a summary line of the call (timestamp + functionName + arg 1 + arg 2 + ...) to an R object. So far I use this approach as it suits my purpose well enough but there are probably better ways, like defining a function that could take each of your functions as an argument and do both the call and the log update. Maybe there are also subtleties to be taken into account depending on what you plan to do with your logs (like re-run the commands)

Looking around I also found out about the log4r package that should help with the warnings/errors.

I too indeed remain curious of other/better ways to log what is going during a shiny session (ui-wise and server-wise) but I hope this helps a bit.

Well, I answer myself just in case anyone has a similar issue, I solved placing in server the following ...

  observe({
    popular <- input$popular
    updateTextInput(session,"stock",value = popular)

Solved via javascript.

I changed moveFocusOnTab.js to:

jQuery(document).ready(function(){
  var elementTags = ace.edit("elementTags");
elementTags.commands.bindKey("Tab",null);
elementTags.commands.bindKey("Shift+Tab",null);
    }
);

I had seen that editor.commands.bindKey() was the obvious solution on many threads but I always failed to capture the editor object as I didn't know of ace.edit().

Bastien

messages.subject: Re: plotOutput seems to make ui ignore conditionalPanels
messages.subject_clean: plotOutput seems to make ui ignore conditionalPanels
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I believe it is not possible to use the same outputId several times in ui.R and that it is the main reason for your trouble (maybe the styling and formatting adds to the problem but I couldn't tell).

It is probably not best practice but I usually "multiple-assign" a plot in server.R if I want to call it more than once in ui.R
See below, I did that for GraphOne & Graphfive in server.R and it should work. But if for instance you call GrapheOne in each of the three panel it shouldn't work.

ui.R

library(shiny)

fluidPage(
  fluidRow(
    column(7),

    #Selects GraphNum
    column(3,
           radioButtons("GraphNum", "How Many Graphs?", c("One", "Two", "Three"), selected="One", inline=T)
    )
  ),

  #creates rows and columns for graphs

  conditionalPanel(
    condition="input.GraphNum=='One'",
    fluidRow(

             plotOutput("GraphOne")
    )
  ),

  conditionalPanel(
    condition="input.GraphNum=='Two'",
    fluidRow(
      plotOutput("GraphTwo"),
      plotOutput("GraphThree")
    )

  ),

  conditionalPanel(
    condition="input.GraphNum=='Three'",

    fluidRow(
      plotOutput("GraphFor"),
      plotOutput("GraphFive"),
      plotOutput("GraphSix")
    )
  )
)

server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$GraphFive<-output$GraphOne <- renderPlot({

    plot(c(1:10))
  })

  output$GraphTwo <- renderPlot({
    barplot(c(1:5))
  })

  output$GraphThree <- renderPlot(
    plot(c(2:5))
  )

  output$GraphFor <- renderPlot({
    plot(c(10:1))
  })

  output$GraphSix <- renderPlot({
    plot(c(5:2))
  })
})

I hope that helps,

Bastien

I would like to save the generated d3Pie's plot as a downloadble png and ultimately insert into an excel wb report I'm making using xlsx package. I am able to make a report with inserted ggplot, now just want to upgrade by ggplot to an d3Pie:

    outfile <- tempfile(fileext='.png')

    png(outfile, width=900, height=250)

    dev.off()

    addPicture(file=outfile, radsheet, scale = 1, startRow = start.row+2,startColumn = 3)

output$downloadData_summary_org <- downloadHandler(

  filename = function() {paste(input$Org,".xlsx",sep='') },

  content = function(file){

    #Select Department

    table<-input$SummaryReportBox_Org

    #save, format, rename and download workbook

      saveWorkbook(

https://gist.github.com/withr/59cc48edc1658b61ea4e

messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I would like to read (and periodically poll) a log file that the user has selected through the gui (using, e.g., choose.files()).  Unfortunately, the filePath argument to reactiveFileReader does not allow the use of reactives.  So something like

file_contents <- reactiveFileReader(1000, session, filePath = myfile(), readFunc = scan, what = "character", sep = "\n")

where myfile() is some reactive that returns the file name as a  string will fail with the message:

Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext() :
  Operation not allowed without an active reactive context. (You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive expression or observer.)

How can I get a value for the filePath which is chosen by the user but is not a reactive?

Some constraints on acceptable solutions:
1) The name of the log file will change every time the app is used.
2) The user can't type the log file name in using textInput or the like because I am generating the file dynamically, nor do I want to deal with potential typos.

A reproducible example is below.

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
    headerPanel("Reactive File Reader"),
    sidebarPanel(
        actionButton("pick_file", "Pick File"),
        verbatimTextOutput("pick_file")
    ),
    mainPanel(
        textOutput("file_contents")
    )
)

server <- function(input, output, session){
    file_name <- eventReactive(
        input$pick_file,
        file.choose()
    )

    output$pick_file <- renderText(
        file_name()
    )

    file_contents <- reactiveFileReader(1000, session, filePath = file_name(),
                                         readFunc = scan, what = "character",sep = "\n")

    output$file_contents <- renderText(file_contents())

}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

Thanks,

Ted

messages.subject: Re: Shiny.onInputChange is suppressing replicate keypress keys
messages.subject_clean: Shiny.onInputChange is suppressing replicate keypress keys
messages.body_plain:
I think what's happening is not that shiny is "suppressing" the keypress events, but the way reactivity works in shiny means that things don't get triggered if the reactive hasn't changed. In you case, you're setting the "key_press" input to a specific key, so whenever that key changes, shiny triggers a reactive event. But if the JavaScript layer tells shiny "the 'g' key was pressed" and on shiny's end "g" is already the value of that variable, then it doesn't do anything.

So it makes sense why this is happening, but I agree that it'd be nice to be able to force shiny to not ignore even when the value is the same. I have an open issue on shiny on github for this https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/928

messages.subject: Re: I would need your hints, advices and experience for building bilingual apps.
messages.subject_clean: I would need your hints, advices and experience for building bilingual apps.
messages.body_plain:
Hi everybody,

I'd like to finish this thread with my conclusions. First of all, I can't see nothing that relates performance with the use of render**
to translate the texts. But there is something irregular with MathJax: if you need to use it for strings containing latex code, you
have to put withMathJax() once in ui.R, and likely again inside the render**() function. Otherwise, you will obtain strange results.

With regard to the original subject of my question, I managed to sort it out like this:
the texts are written in a UTF-8 ascii file, with three columns separated by tabs: label, sentence in English, sentence in Spanish. Don't write double backslash (\\) for latex since R will double each one. I haven't used excel to write the texts, the csv, tab-separated version included quotes ("), arbitrarily put by excel! (well, probably excel did it for some reason, but I couldn't guess it)
server.R includes the line. .L = read.table(<<file with texts>>, header=FALSE, sep='\t', quote="", row.names=1, colClasses=rep("character", 3))
it also includes the code
>   .E <- reactiveValues(d = 1)  #active language and default
>   tr <- function(stringId) {
>         .L[stringId, .E$d]
>   }
ui.R begins with: Sys.setlocale("LC_ALL", "es_ES.UTF-8") #to be sure that accents in text will be allowed in plots, thanks Grégoire
Put two flags in the top right corner with (the images have to be in the www folder):
>   absolutePanel(
>     top = 0, right = 0, width=80, fluidRow(actionButton("eng", img(src='uk-icon.png'), style="margin:0;padding:0;"),
>                                            actionButton("spa", img(src='Spain-icon.png'), style="margin:0;padding:0;"))
>   ),
Write two observers in server.R to update the active language:
>   observeEvent(input$eng, {    .E$d=1   })
>   observeEvent(input$spa, {    .E$d=2   })
Replace the literal strings by calls to textOutput or uiOutput, with their correspondent render** in server.R. Example:
uiOutput("parrafo"),
output$parrafo = renderText( { tr("parrafo") } )
Hope it helps to others. Regards,

JA

El viernes, 30 de octubre de 2015, 18:25:17 (UTC+1), José Antonio González escribió:

> I've written already some twenty apps of considerable size, almost all of them in Spanish, but I'm considering to include an English
> version. I've discarded a second copy with texts in English, because of expected problems in maintenance of two versions. I'd like
> to have a language selector in the same app, and swap the texts dynamically.
>
> However, after some tests with an app, complex enough for finding different kind of difficulties, I give up. Inexplicably at least for me,
> the two-language version was making its way until a point where it was behaving unpredictably. Some parts (texts or plots) don't
> appear but if I refresh the page in the browser (I'm using a remote server, not Rstudio), it can appear complete, perhaps... Even
> worse, sometimes the load finishes with an error message, but after refreshing the page loads partially or maybe totally.
>
> I have to explain that this behaviour has not appeared at some critical point. I was advancing slowly, writing small pieces of code
> and checking them carefully before facing another piece. The first times I noticed that the error was not a real error I thought that
> the reason could be a mismatch between the remote server and my computer, and the upload was not complete when I tried to
> refresh the page (it would be strange anyway, since the files are really small).
>
> As I was advancing in the implementation of the two-language version, obviously the program was increasing in complexity. I wonder
> if this can have influence in the app behaviour: I had to convert a number of simple p('blablabla'), HTML('blablabla') and widgets in
> renderText and renderUI calls (because of the language dependency), BUT it would be hard to accept that functions like that are
> able to degrade the program so much.
>
> So I think that I should return to the starting point, and adopt a different paradigm. I've sought a bit about the topic, but it seems
> that translations are not very common, or they don't pose any problem normally. In my case, my initial strategy is:

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

The icon should display, but you're not using a correct name/syntax ;)
You can display this icon this way :
      numericInput("standardincome",
                   label = h4("What is your monthly household income?", icon("info-circle")),

                   value = "0", min=0),

To add a tooltip, the easier is to use the shinyBS package :
library(shinyBS)
and then, you can display it this way :

      numericInput("standardincome2",
                   label = h4("What is your monthly household income?", tipify(icon("info-circle"), title = "my tooltip content")),
                   value = 0, min=0),

Or, you could also add the tooltip on the numeric input itself, this way :

      numericInput("standardincome3", label = h4("What is your monthly household income?"), value = 0, min=0),
      bsTooltip(id = "standardincome3", title = "tooltip content", placement = "right")

You can find those in this gist : https://gist.github.com/RCura/2e4e2fe6b02a0c80adad / and run it with : runGist("2e4e2fe6b02a0c80adad")

HTH,

Robin

weightvar <- c("",names(mydata()$df.raw))

out <- calcMDscores(data = mydata()$df.raw, util.vars = utilvars, weight.var = wgtvar,

            if(input$Weightvariable == "") {wgtvar <- NULL} else {

messages.subject: Puzzling behaviour in Shiny: t-statistics calculated twice and differently?!
messages.subject_clean: Puzzling behaviour in Shiny: t-statistics calculated twice and differently?!
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I have a rather strange thing going on, and I cannot find the cause. Although it is not a real 'problem', I am intrigued to know 'why?'.

In short:
This Shiny app (for now) allows the user to draw increasing sample sizes from a normal distribution. It then plots a histogram for each given sample size and calculates the accompanying t-statistic.

The strange thing:
When you fire up the app (and keep the default settings), you will notice in the console (assuming you use RStudio) that when you press the 'Press me' button the second time, the t-statistic is calculated twice. And this keeps occuring when you continue to press the button. I would expect from my own scripts that it should only be calculated once?
Also, the two t-statistic values are always different, which makes me even more puzzled on how R/Shiny computes the first* value.

*I know for sure that the second value is the right one, as I checked it manually with the following code:

sample_size <- 2 # You can increase this number to manually 'simulate' the Shiny App's 'Press me' button
set.seed(123)
data <- rnorm(sample_size, 0, 1)
t_statistic <- (mean(data) - 0) / (sd(data) / sqrt(sample_size))
t_statistic # Check this value with the second t-statistic value after you pressed the 'Press me' button the second time

Here are the accompanying scripts:

#### Launch script ####

install.packages("shiny")

library(shiny)

setwd("") # Set working directory

runApp("", display.mode = "showcase") # Create a folder to store the app scripts

#### ui.R ####

shinyUI(fluidPage(

  # Title of Shiny app
  titlePanel("My World-dominating Shiny App"),

  # sidebarLayout() embodies the widget and output panels
  sidebarLayout(

    # sidebarPanel() displays all widgets
    sidebarPanel(

      # Hypothesis test widgets
      sliderInput(inputId = "h0",
                  label = "What should the null hypothesis mean value be?",
                  min = -10,
                  max = 10,
                  value = 0),

      # helpText() displays information in the app ui
      helpText("Set the desired value by which to increase the sample size
               with each step. Then keep pressing the almighty 'Press me'
               button to see some black magic."),

      # Press the almighty button below to manually increase sample size by 1, 10 or 50 (depending on your choice)

      # Widgets to increase sample size manually and the size of the increase
      fluidRow(

        column(7, radioButtons(inputId = "step_size",
                               label = "Sample size",
                               choices = c("1",
                                           "10",
                                           "50"),
                               inline = TRUE)
        ),

        column(5, actionButton(inputId = "step",
                               label = "Press me")
        )

      )

    ),

    # Output panel displaying the reactive outputs
    mainPanel(plotOutput("plot"),
              #tableOutput("table")
              textOutput("text"))
  )
))

#### server.R ####

shinyServer(function(input,output){

  ## Object values for server.R (in order of appearance)

  seed <- 123 # Setting the seed for set.seed()
  # number of samples drawn from rnorm()
  sample_size <- reactive({(input$step * as.integer(input$step_size))})
  # Reactive input by user, determining the mean of the drawn samples
  sample_mean <- reactive({input$h0})
  sample_sd <- 1 # Standard deviation of the drawn samples
  true_mean <- 0 # The true mean you want to test your H0 with

  ## Reactive outputs are returned to ui.R

  output$plot <- renderPlot({

    # If/else statement for plotting histogram, text and t-statistic value

    if (sample_size() == 0){

      # If sample_size is 0, then an 'empty histogram' is plotted
      plot(NULL,
           main = paste("Histogram of sampled data \nSample size:", sample_size()),
           xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1),
           xlab = "Sample values", ylab = "Frequency",
           bty = "n")

      # Text indicating that t-statistic cannot be computed
      output$text <- renderText({
        print("Need sample size > 1 to calculate t-statistic (1)")
      })

    }

    else { # If sample_size is not equal to 0,
           # then a histogram of the sampled data is plotted

      set.seed(seed) # set.seed() to ensure replicable rnorm() data
      data <- rnorm(sample_size(), sample_mean(), sample_sd) # Sampling the data

      # Plot the histogram of the data
      hist(data,
           main = paste("Histogram of sampled data \nSample size:", sample_size()),
           xlab = "Sample values", ylab = "Frequency",
           col = "gray")

      output$text <- renderText({

        # Text indicating that t-statistic cannot be computed
        if (sample_size() < 2){
          print("Need sample size > 1 to calculate t-statistic (2)")
        }

        # Calculate t-statistic and print its value
        else {

          data_mean <- mean(data) # Calculating the mean of the data
          data_sd <- sd(data) # Calculating the standard deviation of the data
          # Calculate t-statistic
          t_statistic <- (data_mean - true_mean) / (data_sd / sqrt(sample_size()))
          print(paste("t-statistic value =", t_statistic, "(3)"))

        }

      })

    }

  })

})

All help is much appreciated :)

Cheers

messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

this is my first post here and since several weeks I am working on a shiny app which since till now was no big problem. Google could always point me where to continue to read.

Just currently I am facing a limitation in my understanding how shiny works. Hope you can help me further.

Function description:
File is uploaded and stored in filedata(). I can access all date there and could do all my plots. Except my latest idea and wish. For ggplot I like to sort my data by using row.names.

The original R code:
test$group <- row.names(test)
test.m <- melt(test, id.vars = "group")

I do it step by step and then let me return the values in a table to see if my approach works.
Unfortunately I could not even complete the first step and found out with google that in reactive elements I cannot add a row or column.

My first approach was:
boxplotdata1 <- reactive({
  filedata()$group <- row.names(filedata())
})

Ok, as no rows and columns can be added it cannot work.

Can someone please point me to the correct approach or list the functions which could apply?

Thank you,
Karl

  #Drop down for user to choose the column with the weights:

      output$Weightvariable <- renderUI({

            if(is.null(input$datafile)){return()}

            weightvar <- c("", names(mydata()$df.raw))

            selectInput('Weightvariable', 'Pick column with weights (optional)', choices = weightvar,

                        selected = NULL, multiple = FALSE)

      })

But once the user selects one of the column names in the pull-down - it's impossible to "deselect it" (so that the box is empty again). Something is always selected now.

Any hints?

Thanks a lot!

This body of code is not subsettable so make_list$time fails.

To return the result of a function in R, you must follow the function name with a pair of parentheses, (). If you add these parentheses to the call above, R will use $time to subset the list returned by make_fun(), which produces a valid result.

Correction: It should be make_list() instead of make_fun()

X2 <- list(X[2,1])
for (i in 2:length(X[,2])) {
  X[i] <- X[i,1]
}

which takes its time...

Is there any more efficient way of doing this?

Thanks in advance,
António

messages.subject: Stacked DYGraph
messages.subject_clean: Stacked DYGraph
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to switch my dygraph to a stacked dygraph, but it only plots one of the 10 series.

Does anyone know what is causing the issue. My code is below and screenshots of before/after are attached.

Before:
dygraph(classificationplot, main = "Classification Topic Trend") %>%
    dyOptions(colors = c(clrs2[length(clrs2)],clrs2[1:length(clrs2)-1])) %>%
    dyLegend(show = "onmouseover",width="675") %>%
    dyAxis("y", label = "Count of Feedback") %>%
    dyAxis("x", label = "Time") %>%
    dyRangeSelector()

Aftter:
dygraph(classificationplot, main = "Classification Topic Trend") %>%
    dyOptions(stackedGraph = TRUE,colors = c(clrs2[length(clrs2)],clrs2[1:length(clrs2)-1])) %>%
    dyLegend(show = "onmouseover",width="675") %>%
    dyAxis("y", label = "Count of Feedback") %>%
    dyAxis("x", label = "Time") %>%
    dyRangeSelector()

Thanks,
Logan

messages.subject: Setting up a Bridged Connection on a VM for Shiny Server?
messages.subject_clean: Setting up a Bridged Connection on a VM for Shiny Server?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to deploy my Shiny Application over a Shiny Server of a CentOS 6.7 Virtual Machine.  I am connecting through a corporate proxy.

In order for me to direct visitors to the Shiny Web App, I require a Static IP Address for the Virtual Machine and a Bridged Network Connection between the host LAN and the guest LAN.

I am having some trouble setting up the bridged connection in my Virtual Machine.  My confusion comes about when I am configuring the subnet mask and default gateway for the Virtual Machine.

When I set the settings for the bridged connection:
Should the subnet mask be the same or different as the subnet mask of the host?
My subnet mask for the host is 255.255.254.0
Should the default gateway be the same or different as the default gateway of the host?
If there is anyone who has configured a Virtual Machine and Bridged Network Connection for their Shiny App, could you please share how your network is set up?

Thanks for the help,

Nick

messages.subject: Observe events related to programmatically generated inputs with variable names
messages.subject_clean: Observe events related to programmatically generated inputs with variable names
messages.body_plain:
Hi all!
I want to describe my issue and ask for help of the community.

I am trying to create an example of a ShinyApp that allows to automatically generate UI inputs for some scalars provided in a named list. For example, I feed my App with this list:
method <- list('Method name' = "My Great Method",
                      'Post process' = TRUE,
                      'Iterations' = 20).

The App should scan this list and create an input for each element of the list. Ids of the inputs should be set to be equal to the tranformed names of the elements in the list (e.g. lowercase and without whitespace). This part is solved programmatically by me. But how to react on changes in these inputs? I do not know, in general, names of these inputs and therefore can't use them in an observe() to implement reactive behaviour...

I hope I described everything clearly and recieve an answer soon. Thank you in advance!

messages.subject: observeEvent does not seem to depend on its first argument changing state?
messages.subject_clean: observeEvent does not seem to depend on its first argument changing state?
messages.body_plain:
This question is related to other posts on clearing Shiny app inputs but I can't find guidance yet that explains the behavior I'm seeing.

here is the shiny app example shiny::runGist("e1c0482c22348d934e71")

The example app has a submit and clear button to allow repeated entry of data by the user.   The real app is connected to a Google Sheet which accumulates records. Each record has many elements (names, dates, etc); it also connects to SurveyMonkey API if certain conditions are met--all that functionality is working.

I'm just hung up on the submit and clear logic.

What I expect to have happen in the example app:

users enters name and clicks Submit.   Data table updates.  After the Clear button is clicked, the shinyjs::reset function clears the text input field.   From the help file for the reset function:

"Reset any input element back to its original value. You can either reset one specific input at a time by providing the id of a shiny input, or reset all inputs within an HTML tag by providing the id of an HTML tag.

Reset can be performed on any traditional Shiny input widget, which includes: textInput, numericInput, sliderInput, selectInput, selectizeInput, radioButtons, dateInput, dateRangeInput, checkboxInput, checkboxGroupInput. Buttons are not supported, meaning that you cannot use this function to reset the value of an action button back to 0."

So, when the reset function executes, I expect the state of the Submit button to stay in its current state (it has been clicked ONCE).

The submit_check1 reactive function executes when the Clear button is clicked as the state of the input$champ_name has changed; it prints out the error message "Enter name".

(This is acceptable behavior for now.)

Here's the part I don't understand:

it looks like the reactive functions sheet_confirmation and df1_out are both executing once the name box is filled in, even though these functions are contained within an observeEvent function.  I thought the observeEvent function requires a change in state of submit button to execute, given its first argument.   In other words, I expect to have to click the Submit button to get those functions to execute but that's not the case.

Can anyone explain why?

Thanks

here is the shiny app example shiny::runGist("e1c0482c22348d934e71")

and here is the script   app.R:
#######################################################################
#test app to load the form and clear it for second record entry
#Kevin Little, Ph.D.  18 Nov 2015

require(shiny)
require(shinyapps)
require(shinyjs)

#local df taking the place of a Google sheet
df1 <- data.frame(name="name1", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

ui <- fluidPage(

   useShinyjs(),
   div(id="form_app",
      textInput(
        inputId = "champ_name",
        label   = "Your name",
        value   = "")
  ),
  actionButton(inputId = "submit", label="Submit"),
  actionButton(inputId = "ClearAll", label= "Clear"),
  hr(),
  textOutput("sheet_confirmation"),
  tableOutput("table_output")
)

server <- function(input, output){

  submit_check1 <- reactive({
      champ_name <- input$champ_name
      conditions_met <- champ_name != ''

      if (conditions_met) {
            out <- list(submit = TRUE, error_message = NULL)
      }
      else {
            out <- list(submit = FALSE)
            if(champ_name== '') error_message <- "Enter name"
            out$error_message <- error_message
      }
      return(out)
    })
   #This is where I expect to need input$submit to change state before the functions
    #sheet_confirmation and df1_out execute.
    observeEvent(input$submit, {
        sheet_confirmation <- reactive({
        champ_name    <- input$champ_name
        conditions <- submit_check1()
         if(conditions$submit) {
           out <- sprintf("Table updated")
         }
                     else {
            out <- conditions$error_message
          }
         out
      })

        df1_out <- reactive({
        champ_name <- input$champ_name
        conditions <- submit_check1()
        if(conditions$submit) {
          output_sheet_row <- data.frame(name=champ_name)
          #add a row to the data frame
          df1 <- rbind.data.frame(df1,output_sheet_row)
        }
        return(df1)
      })

      output$sheet_confirmation <- renderText(sheet_confirmation())
      output$table_output <- renderTable(df1_out())
    })

      observeEvent(input$ClearAll, {
      reset("form_app")
    })
  }

shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.body_plain:
OK, couple of things here. The reset button is a little bit of a red herring; you can see that even if you don't click reset, once you've hit Submit changing the name using any method will cause the outputs to update.

Your code would make sense if output$foo <- renderBar(...) meant "Update the output 'foo' with the value returned by renderBar(...)". But that's not what output$foo <- renderBar(...) means; it means, "This here is a recipe for rendering a Bar, it should be used continually from now on to populate the 'foo' output." So while the line `output$sheet_confirmation <- renderText(sheet_confirmation())` is only executed when the submit button is clicked, that's enough to keep sheet_confirmation up to date from then on.

Similarly, just because these reactive expressions sheet_confirmation and table_output happen to be created inside an observeEvent, they themselves are just regular reactive expressions--when their dependencies (input$champ_name) changes, they invalidate.

If you find yourself either creating a reactive expression or assigning an output slot inside of an observe() or an observeEvent(), it's almost always a sign that you're on the wrong track.

I've posted a fixed version here: https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/9cadfad7751f20cd957a It uses a champ_name eventReactive to wrap input$champ_name. I also do validation there, which means we don't need sheet_confirmation anymore. See http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/validation.html and https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7sQ6AEDFjZ4 for more on validation.

Thank you Joe foe clear explanation and sample code turned around very fast.   I follow what you're saying and now have a better understanding of reactive events.   Using the eventReactive function works great.   Starting to build out the real app.  than you again!

On Wednesday, November 18, 2015 at 3:44:46 PM UTC-6, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> OK, couple of things here. The reset button is a little bit of a red herring; you can see that even if you don't click reset, once you've hit Submit changing the name using any method will cause the outputs to update.
>
> Your code would make sense if output$foo <- renderBar(...) meant "Update the output 'foo' with the value returned by renderBar(...)". But that's not what output$foo <- renderBar(...) means; it means, "This here is a recipe for rendering a Bar, it should be used continually from now on to populate the 'foo' output." So while the line `output$sheet_confirmation <- renderText(sheet_confirmation())` is only executed when the submit button is clicked, that's enough to keep sheet_confirmation up to date from then on.
>
> Similarly, just because these reactive expressions sheet_confirmation and table_output happen to be created inside an observeEvent, they themselves are just regular reactive expressions--when their dependencies (input$champ_name) changes, they invalidate.
>
> If you find yourself either creating a reactive expression or assigning an output slot inside of an observe() or an observeEvent(), it's almost always a sign that you're on the wrong track.
>
> I've posted a fixed version here: https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/9cadfad7751f20cd957a It uses a champ_name eventReactive to wrap input$champ_name. I also do validation there, which means we don't need sheet_confirmation anymore. See http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/validation.html and https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7sQ6AEDFjZ4 for more on validation.

>

Buttons are not supported, meaning that you cannot use this function to reset the value of an action button back to 0."
> >
> > So, when the reset function executes, I expect the state of the Submit button to stay in its current state (it has been clicked ONCE).
> >
> > The submit_check1 reactive function executes when the Clear button is clicked as the state of the input$champ_name has changed; it prints out the error message "Enter name".

I thought the observeEvent function requires a change in state of submit button to execute, given its first argument.   In other words, I expect to have to click the Submit button to get those functions to execute but that's not the case.
> >

messages.body_plain:
Auto reply !
I found a solution, I explain it here, maybe it will help somebody in the future...
I found a link for the shini-server.conf file here :
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/wiki/Building-Shiny-Server-from-Source

Here is the command line to download this file :
sudo wget https://raw.github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/master/config/upstart/shiny-server.conf -O /etc/init/shiny-server.conf

Then I add this line after the description line of the shiny-server.conf file because some UTF8 character were not understood :

env LANG=en_US.UTF-8

And now the "sudo start shiny-server" command line works fine...
Hope this help

messages.subject: Announcement: Stack traces!
messages.subject_clean: Announcement: Stack traces!
messages.body_plain:
We've made a simple but significant improvement to error handling in Shiny 0.12.2.9006. Errors now have stack traces!

Adding stack traces touched a fair amount of low-level code in Shiny, so I'd greatly appreciate it if you could upgrade to the development version (devtools::install_github("rstudio/shiny")) and let me know if you see any problems. We're hoping to release to CRAN in the coming weeks.

Consider this buggy app.R file:

>  1: library(shiny)
>  2: library(ggplot2)
>  3:
>  4: ui <- fluidPage(
>  5:   plotOutput("plot")
>  6: )
>  7:
>  8: server <- function(input, output, session) {
>  9:   mydata <- reactive({
> 10:     head(25, cars)
> 11:   })
> 12:
> 13:   output$plot <- renderPlot({
> 14:     ggplot(mydata(), aes(speed, dist)) + geom_point()
> 15:   })
> 16: }
> 17:
> 18: shinyApp(ui, server)

Using the latest CRAN version of Shiny, running this app gives you output like this:

> > shinyApp(ui, server)
>
> Listening on http://127.0.0.1:7416
> Error : length(n) == 1L is not TRUE

And that's it--no clue where the error originated.

After installing the latest development version of Shiny the output becomes:

> Listening on http://127.0.0.1:6212
> Warning: Error in : length(n) == 1L is not TRUE
> Stack trace (innermost first):
>     96: stopifnot
>     95: head.default
>     94: head
>     93: reactive mydata [~/app.R#10]
>     82: mydata
>     81: ggplot
>     80: renderPlot [~/app.R#14]
>     72: output$plot
>      5: <Anonymous>
>      4: do.call
>      3: print.shiny.appobj
>      2: print
>      1: source

The stack trace can be read from the bottom up: source() called print(), which called print.shiny.appobj(), which called do.call(), etc.

Generally you'll want to scan from the top down and find the first (i.e. innermost, i.e. most recent) call that comes from your project files--in this case, frame 93 implicates line 10 of app.R, which has "head(25, cars)". Ah, we've reversed the order of the arguments, it should've been "head(cars, 25)".

Notice that the numbers in the stack trace above aren't contiguous; it's missing entries for 6-71, 73-79, and 83-92. Shiny has a lot of internal plumbing, most of which is just not that interesting when you're trying to debug a problem in your app, so we try to hide uninteresting parts of the stack trace. If you suspect that useful information is being hidden, you can turn off the hiding with this option:

> options(shiny.fullstacktrace = TRUE)

Hope you find this change useful!

-joe

messages.subject: Re: append to output?
messages.subject_clean: append to output?
messages.body_plain:
Right, but that doesn't have anything to do with shiny, then.
It's a simple matter of defining a button with something like this, in the body:

<input id="goButton" type="button" value="clickme" />

Then use the mentioned code, in the external javascript file which needs to be mentioned in the <head> part:

$(document).ready(function(){

    $("#goButton").click(function(e){
      $('#result').animate({
        scrollTop: $('#result')[0].scrollHeight
      }, 1000);
    });

})

If you don't understand how this works, there are many examples and tutorials on W3Schools.
I hope it helps,
Adrian

messages.body_plain:
What you're asking for is essentially dynamic scoping <http://c2.com/cgi/wiki?DynamicScoping> and if you want that, you may as well just use a global variable. It doesn't necessarily have to be in the global environment, you can create an environment in your package called e.g. "global" and store global-ish values in it. We do this in a number of places in Shiny.

Here's an example of how we make it easy to get at the current "session" (a.k.a. "reactive domain") from anywhere in Shiny without having to pass it around manually:
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/R/globals.R#L2 <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/R/globals.R>
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/R/reactive-domains.R#L67-L103
?domains

In your case though, I can't help but wonder whether you should just pass the data around using normal function arguments. The global stuff is not that easy to get right when you have multiple clients simultaneously connected.

On Monday, 23 November 2015 11:03:24 UTC-8, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> We've made a simple but significant improvement to error handling in Shiny 0.12.2.9006. Errors now have stack traces!
>
> Adding stack traces touched a fair amount of low-level code in Shiny, so I'd greatly appreciate it if you could upgrade to the development version (devtools::install_github("rstudio/shiny")) and let me know if you see any problems. We're hoping to release to CRAN in the coming weeks.
>
> Consider this buggy app.R file:
>
> >  1: library(shiny)
> >  2: library(ggplot2)
> >  3:
> >  4: ui <- fluidPage(
> >  5:   plotOutput("plot")
> >  6: )
> >  7:
> >  8: server <- function(input, output, session) {
> >  9:   mydata <- reactive({
> > 10:     head(25, cars)
> > 11:   })
> > 12:
> > 13:   output$plot <- renderPlot({
> > 14:     ggplot(mydata(), aes(speed, dist)) + geom_point()
> > 15:   })
> > 16: }
> > 17:
> > 18: shinyApp(ui, server)
>
> Using the latest CRAN version of Shiny, running this app gives you output like this:
>
> > > shinyApp(ui, server)
> >
> > Listening on http://127.0.0.1:7416
> > Error : length(n) == 1L is not TRUE
>
> And that's it--no clue where the error originated.
>
> After installing the latest development version of Shiny the output becomes:
>
> > Listening on http://127.0.0.1:6212
> > Warning: Error in : length(n) == 1L is not TRUE
> > Stack trace (innermost first):
> >     96: stopifnot
> >     95: head.default
> >     94: head
> >     93: reactive mydata [~/app.R#10]
> >     82: mydata
> >     81: ggplot
> >     80: renderPlot [~/app.R#14]
> >     72: output$plot
> >      5: <Anonymous>
> >      4: do.call
> >      3: print.shiny.appobj
> >      2: print
> >      1: source
>
> The stack trace can be read from the bottom up: source() called print(), which called print.shiny.appobj(), which called do.call(), etc.
>
> Generally you'll want to scan from the top down and find the first (i.e. innermost, i.e. most recent) call that comes from your project files--in this case, frame 93 implicates line 10 of app.R, which has "head(25, cars)". Ah, we've reversed the order of the arguments, it should've been "head(cars, 25)".
>
> Notice that the numbers in the stack trace above aren't contiguous; it's missing entries for 6-71, 73-79, and 83-92. Shiny has a lot of internal plumbing, most of which is just not that interesting when you're trying to debug a problem in your app, so we try to hide uninteresting parts of the stack trace. If you suspect that useful information is being hidden, you can turn off the hiding with this option:
>
> > options(shiny.fullstacktrace = TRUE)
>
> Hope you find this change useful!
>
> -joe

I'm not sure how to use your suggestions about 'reactive domain' and where to put them (in the package function code or in server.R?). How this this allow me to connect a users environment to the package environment? As a simple example of what I'm looking for, I'd like `state_init`, which is a function exported by the R-package, to have access to `r_state` which is tied to a specific shiny user.

state_init <- function(inputvar, init = "") {
  if (is.null(r_state[[inputvar]])) init else r_state[[inputvar]]
}

When the app is run on a server I make this work by sourcing all of the package R-code inside server.R. However when the package is loaded and in the search path this doesn't work well.

On Monday, November 23, 2015 at 3:51:50 PM UTC-8, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> What you're asking for is essentially dynamic scoping <http://c2.com/cgi/wiki?DynamicScoping> and if you want that, you may as well just use a global variable. It doesn't necessarily have to be in the global environment, you can create an environment in your package called e.g. "global" and store global-ish values in it. We do this in a number of places in Shiny.
>
> Here's an example of how we make it easy to get at the current "session" (a.k.a. "reactive domain") from anywhere in Shiny without having to pass it around manually:
> https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/R/globals.R#L2 <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/R/globals.R>
> https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/R/reactive-domains.R#L67-L103
> ?domains
>
> In your case though, I can't help but wonder whether you should just pass the data around using normal function arguments. The global stuff is not that easy to get right when you have multiple clients simultaneously connected.
>
> On Mon, Nov 23, 2015 at 3:23 PM Vincent <vincen...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > The main functions in my application are in an R package in the R/ directory. These functions are intended to work both inside and outside of a shiny-app. When calling a function a string is passed with the name of the dataset. Inside shiny that string is used to look-up a dataframe in a reactiveValues object (e.g., r_data).
> >
> > What is the best way to give functions, that , by default, are in their own package environment, access to reactiveValues etc. when called from a Shiny environment? Is it possible to set the shiny environment as the parent environment for functions in a package somehow?
> >
> > I discussed this with @smbache a while back (see link below) and got a working solution. Unfortunately, when running the app locally, I have to make the shiny environment accessible in the global environment which is not ideal.
> >
> > https://github.com/smbache/import/issues/4

I just tried using the dev shiny version of some simple apps I have and I seem to be getting problems with one of them.  I put the code of the app in a gist https://gist.github.com/daattali/d7d72d37229e072f9376
If I run the app using Run App button or using the runApp function, then it works. If I run the app in any way using the CRAN version, then it works. But using the new version, if I manually copy and paste all the lines of the app into the console and run them, this is the output

Listening on http://127.0.0.1:7527
ERROR: [on_request_read] connection reset by peer
Warning: Error in if: missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
Stack trace (innermost first):
    45: srcrefToLabel
    44: reactive
    43: server [#38]
     4: <Anonymous>
     3: do.call
     2: print.shiny.appobj
     1: print
Error in if (m[[1]][1] == -1) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
Warning: Error in nrow: could not find function "prices"
Stack trace (innermost first):
    73: nrow
    72: renderText [#31]
    71: func
    70: output$summaryText
     4: <Anonymous>
     3: do.call
     2: print.shiny.appobj
     1: print
ERROR: [on_request_read] connection reset by peer

The second error seems to be because I'm using a reactive value before it is being defined, so by moving the  `prices <- reactive({...})` statement to the top, it gets fixed, though that was never an issue previously.
The first error is something with `srcrefToLabel` which I'm not familiar with.

Sorry for not giving a minimal reproduceable example, I'm fairly busy but wanted to quickly check it out and not spent too much time on debugging myself, hopefully this is useful

> We've made a simple but significant improvement to error handling in Shiny 0.12.2.9006. Errors now have stack traces!
>
> Adding stack traces touched a fair amount of low-level code in Shiny, so I'd greatly appreciate it if you could upgrade to the development version (devtools::install_github("rstudio/shiny")) and let me know if you see any problems. We're hoping to release to CRAN in the coming weeks.

> Consider this buggy app.R file:
>
> >  1: library(shiny)
> >  2: library(ggplot2)
> >  3:
> >  4: ui <- fluidPage(
> >  5:   plotOutput("plot")
> >  6: )
> >  7:
> >  8: server <- function(input, output, session) {
> >  9:   mydata <- reactive({
> > 10:     head(25, cars)
> > 11:   })
> > 12:
> > 13:   output$plot <- renderPlot({
> > 14:     ggplot(mydata(), aes(speed, dist)) + geom_point()
> > 15:   })
> > 16: }
> > 17:
> > 18: shinyApp(ui, server)
>

>
> > > shinyApp(ui, server)
> >
> > Listening on http://127.0.0.1:7416
> > Error : length(n) == 1L is not TRUE
>
> And that's it--no clue where the error originated.
>
> After installing the latest development version of Shiny the output becomes:
>
> > Listening on http://127.0.0.1:6212
> > Warning: Error in : length(n) == 1L is not TRUE
> > Stack trace (innermost first):
> >     96: stopifnot
> >     95: head.default
> >     94: head
> >     93: reactive mydata [~/app.R#10]
> >     82: mydata
> >     81: ggplot
> >     80: renderPlot [~/app.R#14]
> >     72: output$plot
> >      5: <Anonymous>
> >      4: do.call
> >      3: print.shiny.appobj
> >      2: print
> >      1: source
>
> The stack trace can be read from the bottom up: source() called print(), which called print.shiny.appobj(), which called do.call(), etc.
>
> Generally you'll want to scan from the top down and find the first (i.e. innermost, i.e. most recent) call that comes from your project files--in this case, frame 93 implicates line 10 of app.R, which has "head(25, cars)". Ah, we've reversed the order of the arguments, it should've been "head(cars, 25)".
>
> Notice that the numbers in the stack trace above aren't contiguous; it's missing entries for 6-71, 73-79, and 83-92. Shiny has a lot of internal plumbing, most of which is just not that interesting when you're trying to debug a problem in your app, so we try to hide uninteresting parts of the stack trace. If you suspect that useful information is being hidden, you can turn off the hiding with this option:
>
> > options(shiny.fullstacktrace = TRUE)
>
> Hope you find this change useful!
>
> -joe

I just tried this

library(shiny)

ui <- basicPage(
  plotOutput("plot1", click = "plot_click"),
  verbatimTextOutput("info")
)

server <- function(input, output) {
    output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
        x <- runif(100)
        y <- runif(100)
        xyplot(y~x)
  })

  output$info <- renderText({
    paste0("x=", input$plot_click$x, "\ny=", input$plot_click$y)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

And notice I used xyplot. it worked! Let me see if there are any issues ... I 'm going to guess it wont work with trellis displays ...

On Friday, October 2, 2015 at 2:24:49 PM UTC+1, Andy Kipp wrote:
> GIles,
>
> shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> supports installing private packages from GitHub assuming two things: 1) you installed the package using `devtoos::install_github`, 2) you've linked your shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> account to GitHub and enabled 'private repository access' in the dashboard. Using this method, when you deploy your app we will download the package directly from GitHub.
>
> We currently don't support similar functionality for bitbucket, but this is something we coud look at adding if we get lot of requests for it. It would probably work identically to the way GitHub works.
>
> -Andy
>

> > I can't see how to use shinyapps::deployApp() with private repos - if I put install_bitbucket in ui.R, with authentication, I get an error "ERROR: unable to install packages " and I think the documentation says github only.  But can I install a private repository off github?
> >
> > My workaround at the moment is just to copy the code into the project directory for the app and reference it (source it) there - but this backward step is not very nice and will someday lead to a version control error.
> >

messages.body_plain:
Joe,

I believe the shrinking issue has to do with how the rcharts package applies style info to charts. Whenever an nvd3 chart is rendered it sets the height and with for all of the other nvd3 plots in other tabs in shiny. My apologies that It might take me sometime to create a reproducible example. So for now, I feel like the best solution is probably to learn how to reset the length of C when leaving tab B. Any suggestion how to do that?

Thanks a lot!
Charlotte

messages.body_plain:
In shiny server function:

# One of the few times you'll see me create a non-reactive variable outside
# of a observer that's assigned from within the observer...
lastTab <- NULL
observe({
  on.exit(lastTab <<- input$tab)
  if (identical(lastTab, "B") && !identical(input$tab, "B")) {
    # You're leaving B, adjust C
  }
})

messages.body_plain:
I have an app hosted on the open source shiny server with the below shiny-server.conf file.

# Instruct Shiny Server to run applications as the user "shiny"
run_as shiny;

# Define a server that listens on port 3838
server {
  listen 3838;

  # Define a location at the base URL
  location / {

    # Host the directory of Shiny Apps stored in this directory
    site_dir /srv/shiny-server;

    # Log all Shiny output to files in this directory
    log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;
    app_idle_timeout 10;
    # When a user visits the base URL rather than a particular application,
    # an index of the applications available in this directory will be shown.
    directory_index on;

  }
}
~

Irrespective of the fact that the timeout is set to 10 seconds, it simply does not time out!  I even raised a question on the r studio community and they acknowledged the same.
https://support.rstudio.com/hc/communities/public/questions/206008508-Session-timeout-in-shiny-server

messages.subject: Re: Get D3heatmap Variable on Mouseclick
messages.subject_clean: Get D3heatmap Variable on Mouseclick
messages.body_plain:
Not at the moment, because click means zoom-out. If you must have this functionality, you can fork the repo and replace this block:

https://github.com/rstudio/d3heatmap/blob/3145f89426a438a1b3831053223d1fecf9e18a1c/inst/htmlwidgets/d3heatmap.js#L68-L76

with this code:

        hm.on('click', function(e) {
          Shiny.onInputChange(id + '_click', !e.data ? e.data : {
            label: e.data.label,
            row: x.matrix.rows[e.data.row],
            col: x.matrix.cols[e.data.col]
          });
        });

Then input$outputId_click will give you the row/col data you need.

messages.body_plain:
Ginger, I had the same issue this week, also using shiny::validate in an app that requires jsonlite..

Check the order of your loading packages and whether you get a warning message that shiny::validate is masked by jsonlite::validate.

The validate function in jsonlite is expecting a single argument text string, not the arguments of shiny::validate (and that matches the error message you report).  Loading the shiny package after the jsonlite package will get you the validate function in shiny.    Or explicitly change the function call to explicitly reference the shiny package as shiny::validate

messages.subject: How can i convert ggplot2 to plotly in shiny?
messages.subject_clean: How can i convert ggplot2 to plotly in shiny?
messages.body_plain:
ui.r
library(shiny)
library(plotly)
# Rely on the 'WorldPhones' dataset in the datasets
# package (which generally comes preloaded).
library(datasets)

# Define the overall UI
shinyUI(

  # Use a fluid Bootstrap layout
  fluidPage(

    # Give the page a title
    titlePanel("Telephones by region"),

    # Generate a row with a sidebar
    sidebarLayout(

      # Define the sidebar with one input
      sidebarPanel(
        selectInput("region", "Region:",
                    choices=colnames(WorldPhones)),
        hr(),
        helpText("Data from AT&T (1961) The World's Telephones.")
      ),

      # Create a spot for the barplot
      mainPanel(
        plotlyOutput("phonePlot")
      )

    )
  )
)
server.r
library(shiny)
library(plotly)
# Rely on the 'WorldPhones' dataset in the datasets
# package (which generally comes preloaded).
library(datasets)

# Define a server for the Shiny app
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  # Fill in the spot we created for a plot
  output$phonePlot <- renderPlotly({

    # Render a barplot
   gg<- barplot(WorldPhones[,input$region]*1000,
            main=input$region,
            ylab="Number of Telephones",
            xlab="Year")
  })
p <- ggplotly(gg,session="knitr")
  p
})

Cheers,

Joe

messages.body_plain:
Hi, not sure if this is exactly for your case (depends on the network settings of the host) but based on my setup:
- You have to create a new host-only network adapter in the vm settings
- The IP of this new VM network adapter must be set to static and with the same subnet mask as the host
- I have left the gateway empty

messages.subject: Display of en dashes on shiny.io
messages.subject_clean: Display of en dashes on shiny.io
messages.body_plain:
Hi Everyone,

My application reads in a file (hierarchy.csv) and uses it as a lookup source to create two columns in a datatable.
This datatable is (i) rendered using the DT datatables function and (ii) exported it as results.csv

hierarchy.csv contains text with en dashes. When run locally these display correctly both in the rendered table and in results.csv.
However, when I publish the app to shiny.io <http://shiny.io>, the en dashes are replaced with < 96 >. (I am using the same browser, Firefox, throughout)

I can get the en dashes to display in the rendered table on shiny.io <http://shiny.io> by replacing them in hierarchy.csv with –
However, I then have this character code rather than en dashes in results.csv.

I suspect I need to specify encoding at some point but I am out of my depth in that regard.
How is the shiny.io <http://shiny.io> server set up to deal with special characters?

Any suggestions?

Many thanks

Philip

Jose,

When you download an application bundle, it is a tar.gz file, so if you are on Windows I believe you can open the file with a tool like WinRAR <http://www.rarlab.com/download.htm>. If you are on MacOSX or Unix, you can use tar. Besides that, it looks like there is something wrong with the application dependencies. Once you download the program, you can re-deploy it, which will hopefully resolve the issue.

-Andy

> library(shinydashboard)

>   })
>   output$regression<-renderUI(reg())

> )
